metadata.coverage_note: Reviewed urban/suburban release: 76 ETUSA Lines (50 from the retained registry plus 26 whose identity comes from the evidenced OSM operator match alone, chiefly the 6xx/7xx suburban network the registry never listed, including the three suburban runs into Boumerdes and Tipaza), 8 official ETUS Sidi Bel Abbès Lines, 7 current ETUS Tiaret Lines, 5 official ETUS Béjaïa Lines, 5 official ETUSTO Lines, 5 official ETUS Setif Lines, 5 official ETUS Oum El Bouaghi Lines, 4 official ETUL Laghouat Lines, 4 official ETUS M'Sila Lines, 16 official ETUS Aïn Defla Lines across Aïn Defla, Khemis Miliana and El Attaf, 6 official ETUS Annaba Lines (the numbered routes of its 2026 service program; 19 unnumbered services kept as evidence), 10 official ETUS Tlemcen Lines from its 2026 service program, 1 ETO Oran Line (the numbered route among six ETO published as drawings; five destination-named services kept as evidence), and 1 ETUS Mostaganem Line. Laghouat Line refs and Arabic route names come from two dated Operator programs; duty allocations, vehicles, times and an ambiguous ADL route code remain evidence-only. Oum El Bouaghi identities and Arabic endpoints come from five numbered Operator diagrams; major Stations and distances remain Source evidence, while the unnumbered night loop is evidence-only. Aïn Defla identities come from the Operator's 2025 route artwork and Eid service program; AD-2 has reusable OSM geometry reconciled to that identity, the rest are directory-only. Setif Line identities and Arabic endpoints come from official 2026 Operator artwork; Lines 101, 104 and 106B have reusable OSM geometry reconciled to the announced identities. Lines 105 and 106A remain directory-only because no current public geometry was found. Béjaïa Line identity, endpoints, typed stop counts and service hours come from the Operator API and linked timetable panels; Sidi Bel Abbès identities, endpoints and complete directional departures come from supplied official network/timetable HTML; M'Sila identities, endpoints, ordered Arabic stop names and stop counts come from official route diagrams. Operator-controlled map geometry remains validation-only. OSM supplies reusable geometry where available. Shapes are available for 61 ETUSA, 1 ETUS Aïn Defla, 7 Tiaret, 3 Tizi Ouzou, 3 Setif and 1 Mostaganem Lines. An OSM-identified Line carries source "osm", no published termini, and links every relation its shape was assembled from so a wrong route can be reported or corrected at the origin. Excludes stale Tiaret ref 33 plus unresolved, taxi, non-ETUSA cross/inter-wilaya, unmatched Setif, ETUAD and validation-only geometry.

metadata.coverage_note: Clinics and proximity-care facilities from OpenStreetMap. A community-maintained extract, NOT an official registry: it mixes the public proximity tier (polycliniques, salles de soins, centres de santé) with private clinics and maternities, and coverage is partial and uneven by wilaya. It complements @geoalgeria/sante, which carries the Ministry of Health registry tier (CHU/EPH/EHS/EPSP) that is excluded here. Every OSM element a @geoalgeria/sante hospital-tier record (CHU/EPH/EHS) references is excluded from this package by construction, so no hospital is published twice under the same OSM element. Elements referenced by a sante EPSP record are kept on purpose: there the reference is a geocoding anchor on the entity's seat and the element is usually one of the facilities that EPSP runs, which is this package's population (entity in sante, facility here). sante's remaining records carry no OSM reference at all, so the same physical establishment can still appear in both packages under different coordinates. The two describe different tiers and must never be summed.

provenance_notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-09, the one place this file deliberately departs from upstream OSM: El Aricha (63) was subtracted from Tlemcen (13). El Aricha became its own wilaya in the 2026 reform, carved out of Tlemcen; OSM added the new relation (20815946, ref 63) but never shrank the parent relation (1280702, ref 13), which still spans its pre-reform extent, so 100% of El Aricha also fell inside Tlemcen and a third of the area Tlemcen drew was really El Aricha. Verified against a live Overpass pull on 2026-08-09 (timestamp_osm_base 2026-08-08T16:16:37Z): re-sourcing from OSM reproduces the defect rather than fixing it, which is why the correction lives here. Computed as a polygon difference by scripts/fix-wilaya-overlap.mjs (polygon-clipping), reusing the 24 vertices the two rings already shared, so no sliver was introduced and no territory was lost or gained: Tlemcen 9,098 km2 to 6,083 km2 and El Aricha 3,015 km2 sum back to the original 9,098 km2. Tlemcen went from 127 to 135 vertices; every other feature is byte-identical. Reported by Karim OA (konfo.net) from the Sismoo mobile app, and submitted upstream to OSM. Guarded by test/wilaya-boundaries-disjoint.test.mjs, which fails on the pre-correction geometry.
Imported verbatim from the GeoAlgeria app repo, commit 300cb85 (main), blob 92642be34c678e243e664a55ca7a373dd1f08e94 — byte-identical, geometry untouched.

The OSM extraction itself landed in the app repo on 2026-06-21 in commit f107d6a ('fix: replace GADM wilaya boundaries with OSM data (69 wilayas)'), which records the source (OSM admin_level=4 relations), the licence (ODbL) and the simplification (mapshaper dp 2%, keep-shapes). The bytes have not changed since.

retrieved = 2026-06-21 is the commit date of that extraction and therefore an UPPER BOUND on the Overpass pull date. The file carries no timestamp_osm_base or any other provenance field (properties are `code` only), and no fetch script for it exists in either repo, so the exact pull date cannot be established. It is not a guess at a narrower date.

The commonly quoted '~150 m' figure describes the COORDINATE QUANTISATION (3 decimal places ≈ 111 m in latitude, ≈ 96 m in longitude at 30°N), not the simplification error. Douglas-Peucker at 2% left a median vertex spacing of 3.4 km, so the polygon can depart from the true border by far more than 150 m along any simplified stretch. Treat these as display-grade boundaries (good to about z11), not as a survey-grade border test.

Superseded predecessor: the same file was built from GADM 4.1 before f107d6a; app-repo scripts/prepare-boundaries.mjs still builds that version and must never be re-run. An unverified OSM re-extraction is parked on the app-repo branch chore/osm-boundaries and was deliberately NOT used here.
Data licence is ODbL-1.0 even though the geoalgeria npm package is MIT — the same split the repo already uses for its other OSM-derived packages (ecoles, mosquees, pharmacies, tourisme).
